profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer - UI / Tools
profile.summary:
• A proficient C# developer with 3+ years of experience developing with Unity for games released on PC, consoles, and mobile platforms.
• Have a history of being adaptable in small teams to accomplish a wide array of tasks in UI, server code, gameplay, and third-party integrations.
• Passionate about building games, creating useful tools, and working with emerging tech involving AR and VR.

positions.title: UI Engineer / Generalist
positions.description:
• Worked with APB dev lead to sync PC with console codebases. This involved updating external libraries for many engine customizations, and resolving hundreds of compiler errors brought about by the updates and engine leap from Unreal 3.0 to 3.5. Likewise, I jumped between many different systems of the engine and game to resolve bugs as part of the update and new battle royale mode.
• Implemented VOIP in APB using the Vivox 5 SDK, simplifying how clients interface with the online service and eliminating the need to run a separate voice server.
• Made player analytics in RWBY and Shards queryable by storing meaningful data with ElasticSearch's NEST API
• Supported lead UI engineer on RWBY and Shards in implementing gameplay and menu UIs using UGUI, ensuring as much code could be shared across games, and thus reduce development time.

positions.title: UI Engineer
positions.description:
• Ported Hex from PC to PS4, working with the designer to replace PC-centric UIs and rebuild them from the ground up for quicker navigation, utilizing bumpers for intuitive paging, and taking advantage of selector wheels for fast switching of different filtering/sorting options in the deck editor.
• Implemented UIs for unique additions to the game, like a "siege" mode where players could set up their own gauntlets for others to play against, or an interface that gave players the ability to "fuse" certain cards.
• Shifted initialization of NData’s components to break up large Unity scene hierarchies into more modular pieces and avoid nested prefabs that were prone to cause issues later on.

positions.title: Junior Programmer
positions.description: • Mapped out a trading card game's campaign waypoints, and handled dialogue events using JSON-style scripts.

positions.title: Junior Programmer
positions.description:
• Wrote exporter for in-house C++ based engine to convert text-formatted game data to binary for more efficient loading across all console platforms
• Created various physics-based behaviors for the player damage system and hazardous objects in a space-themed sidescroller. 
• Extended Unity editor for designers to visualize adjustments made to game actors that would affect gameplay (e.g. blast damage radii, line-of-sight cones, direction and point of impact of projectiles).
• Implemented special tiles for a Match 3 game that were designed to help/hinder player progress (e.g. tiles that "infected" adjacent ones, or ones that exploded after a set amount of turns and shielded surrounding tiles).
• Implemented a significant design change to a card game's turn phase rules by reworking a portion of the game's state machine. 

• Scripted game events, set up game audio hooks, and fixed various levels of bugs reported in the database.

positions.title: QA Tester
positions.description:
• Prepared game titles for submissions across multiple platforms (Xbox 360, PS3, Wii, WiiU, and 3DS) by testing against each console's set of standards.
 • Worked in the Mantis bug tracking system to report crashes, broken functionality, visual artifacts, and missing or confusing content to developers.

volunteerExperiences.description:
• Helped lead an international team of volunteer devs and artists to develop a mobile, augmented-reality scavenger hunt for conference attendees using Unity and Vuforia Engine.
• Guided the team through UI development, Unity implementations/best-practices, asset optimization, and worked with the team’s UX/UI designers and artists to create the look and flow of the app.
• Integrated GameSparks to track user progress online and provide analytics across multiple years of the conference.
• Built an editor and components to complement the data-driven design, making it easier for team members to add, edit, and assign game text, and associate AR targets to specific game characters.
• Maintained the project repo, performed code reviews with other developers, and managed game builds for Android and iOS.

projects.title: SIGGRAPH ScavengeAR
projects.description: A mobile, augmented reality scavenger hunt designed to increase attendee engagement with the rest of the SIGGRAPH conference. Developed by an international group of students and professionals from various backgrounds including software engineering, art, and education.
